venue: Automated Software Engineering (Springer journal), vol. 33 (2026), article 38

key_numbers.metric: Pass@3 repairs (ChatGPT-4, with vs without SPVR)
Ablation Pass@3 (ChatGPT-3.5-turbo, with vs without MET info)

structure_gain: Removing MET-derived (AST-diff) syntax info dropped pass@3 from 138/547 to 55/547 on ChatGPT-3.5-turbo, same model/samples/metric (Table 10, Sec 5.4) -- roughly 151% relative gain from the structured syntax cues.
confound_note: Ablation in Table 10 holds model and dataset fixed, varying only whether MET-derived syntax info is in the prompt -- a clean representation-only comparison; the headline comparison to VRepair (Table 5) confounds model/architecture and decoding strategy (pass@3 vs beam size 50).
stop_detail: Generated patches are constrained by matching the parsed output against the identified MET subtree during regeneration (Section 3.4) -- a syntactic well-formedness filter, not semantic or formal verification.
threats_to_datum: C/C++ only; hand-derived extraction rules cover only 61.39% of samples and were mined from under 5% of the dataset (Table 2); correctness judged by string/CodeBLEU match to ground truth, no runtime or semantic verification.

key_numbers.metric: Juliet F1 (CSA warnings, before vs after)

structure_gain: eCPG-based slicing (vs full-file raw context, LLM4FPM-noslice) improves accuracy by +3.02pp and F1 by +1.73pp on the same Qwen2.5-32B model (Table III); the raw-file variant also fails outright on 40 cases due to context-window overflow.
confound_note: RQ3 ablation (Table III) isolates representation by holding the LLM fixed while toggling eCPG-slicing and FARF; the RQ1 comparison to prior SOTA LLM4SA confounds representation with differing prompting strategy and self-consistency voting.
stop_detail: The FARF algorithm formally guarantees completeness of the retrieved dependent-file set via whole-program CPG + file-reference-graph SCC traversal (Section III-C); it verifies coverage of context, not correctness of the slice's judgment.
threats_to_datum: Most real-world false negatives traced to Joern parsing failures (macros, function pointers, #ifdef); slicing granularity is file-level, not function/variable-level; C/C++ only, no cross-language evaluation.

demote_reason: Full text confirms the core contribution is comparing zero-shot reasoning/prompting strategies (Baseline, CoT, Think, Think & Verify) over plain raw-text code -- no structural representation (AST/CFG/CPG/slice) or retrieved knowledge is used at any point. The multi-granularity analysis (single-function vs multi-function-single-file vs multi-file, Section 4.4) is a secondary, uncontrolled scope comparison layered on identical raw-text serialization, not a studied representation/context mechanism, so this is prompt-only work per E1.

structure_gain: vs LLM4SA baseline (broad context, no localized constraint analysis), same GPT-4o-mini/dataset/temperature=0: NPD FPR_R 0.51 -> 0.72 (+41.2% relative, Table 1); vs LLMDFA (exhaustive path traversal): NPD FPR_R 0.35 -> 0.72 (+105.7%).
confound_note: Section 4.4 ablation (NoContext, BatchSol) holds the LLM fixed and varies only presence of iterative agent-driven context retrieval/constraint solving -- a clean isolation; the headline comparisons to LLM4SA/LLMDFA baselines (Table 1) vary both representation and the underlying analysis algorithm together.
stop_detail: The reasoning/solving loop halts when Z3 returns UNSAT or after a max of 5 context-retrieval iterations / 3 solver-error-fix rounds (Sections 3.2.2, 3.3) -- solver-grounded termination, not mere LLM self-report.
threats_to_datum: Ground-truth labeling required ~100 person-hours with only 2 annotators; max context-retrieval depth of 5 may miss deeper dependencies; evaluated on 3 C/C++ projects only, no cross-language evaluation.

structure_gain: vs CWE-DF (LLM-only baseline, no constraint-solving structure): 48-52% accuracy vs VULSOLVER's 96.64-98.41% (Table IV) -- but this is confounded with a different LLM-prompting architecture, not representation alone.
confound_note: Main comparisons (Table IV, vs CodeQL/CWE-DF/Best-Rated-Agent) vary both representation/pipeline and overall system architecture together; the internal ablation (Fig. 4, removing Branch Method Analysis / Context Maintenance modules) also changes pipeline logic, not representation alone -- authors themselves note it is 'not purely representation-only.'
stop_detail: Verification is a final logical check of the derived sink parameter state S_n against Trigger Constraints (Phi_tg) once the last subtask's state is obtained (Sections III-C3, II-D2) -- self-contained symbolic evaluation, no external SMT solver.
threats_to_datum: Still depends on SAST tooling for initial path/taint extraction; critical-type and non-exploitability conditions are hand-defined per vulnerability category; real-world validation limited to 3 projects; results vary by backbone LLM (Kimi-K2 vs GPT-4o differ 7-8%).

datasets: OOD set of 31 post-cutoff CVE-patch pairs
structure_gain: No dataset-wide numeric ablation of context vs no-context is reported; a single qualitative case (Fig. 1/Sec II-A) shows Qwen3-4B misses a null-check bug from caller-only context but succeeds once the callee implementation (interprocedural context) is added -- the effect is not quantified across the benchmark.
confound_note: The headline results (Table III) compare VULPO-4B to baselines using different backbone models/sizes (Qwen3-4B, DeepSeek-V3.1) and different training regimes, so context contribution is confounded with model and optimization-method differences; the RQ6 ablation instead varies RL reward dimensions (outcome/localization/reasoning), not representation content.
stop_detail: LLM-based judges (GPT-OSS-120B, 99.75% judge accuracy) grade outcome/localization/reasoning against the ground-truth CVE description and patch diff to compute the RL reward (Section V-B/V-C, Eq. 3) -- judge-based grounding, not formal verification.
threats_to_datum: Trained/tested only at 4B scale; single language (C/C++); OOD generalization set is only 31 samples; binary/CWE-level labels shown to overestimate true localization/reasoning capability (Section VII-H).

datasets: Tencent industrial dataset: 433 alerts (NPD, DBZ, OOB) from BkCheck SAT

key_numbers.metric: False positive rate among industrial alerts

structure_gain: LLM4PFA (path-constraint hybrid) vs Basic Prompt, same GPT-4o backbone: accuracy 0.50 -> 0.93 (+0.43), FPR_Recall 0.45 -> 0.98 (+0.53) (Table 2).
confound_note: Table 2 pairs each technique with the same LLM backbone per row, reasonably isolating technique effect for that pairing; but overall the study also varies backbone LLM (GPT-4o, Claude-Opus-4, Qwen-3-Coder, DeepSeek-R1) across techniques, and prior learning-based baselines (Devign, ReGVD, LLMAO, LineVul) differ entirely in training data/architecture.
stop_detail: Ground truth established via two-round manual review by developers/code reviewers plus majority voting over 3 LLM runs; no automated or formal verification oracle.
threats_to_datum: Single company (Tencent), single proprietary SAT tool (BkCheck), C/C++ only, 433 alerts over ~10 months from one business division -- limited external validity, explicitly acknowledged by the authors.

structure_gain: Adding interprocedural context (callee/caller code) DEGRADED performance for most models -- e.g. GPT-4.1 Mini F1 dropped 0.8608 -> 0.6753 (Code-Only vs Code+Callees, C, same model/prompt/temperature=0); only Claude Haiku 4.5 was robust. Token usage nearly doubled (+102%) without proportional gains.
confound_note: Clean representation-only ablation: identical model, prompt template, temperature=0, and output length across conditions -- only the amount/type of interprocedural context varies (Code-Only vs +Callees vs +Callers).
stop_detail: No grounding/verification mechanism; this is a pure prompting study -- LLM outputs are parsed via regex and compared to ReposVul ground-truth CVE labels.
threats_to_datum: Dataset has no negative (non-vulnerable) examples, so 'accuracy' is effectively recall; possible training-data contamination from public CVE reports; single-evaluator manual scoring of explanations (RQ4); C++ sample sizes as small as 5-18 excluded from statistical testing.

structure_gain: Removing the structural Control Path (AST/CFG/DFG-derived) drops P-C from 55 to 42 (-23.6% relative) and raises errors from 76 to 89, same GPT-4o backend and test subset (Table 2).
confound_note: Table 2 ablation isolates each of the three context paths (Control/Knowledge/Semantic) with GPT-4o held fixed -- a clean representation-only comparison; Table 1's comparison to VulTrial/ConColl and other baselines confounds representation with differing system architectures.
stop_detail: The Semantic Path is prompt-constrained to describe only directly observable code behaviors, avoiding speculation about programmer intent -- a soft prompting constraint, not a formal or external verification mechanism.
threats_to_datum: Fixed three-path design with no adaptive per-language/per-vulnerability-type selection; no project-specific coding rules or historical patches incorporated; Kotlin evaluation is small (118 functions, 10-round random split) and scope is function-level only.

datasets: Merged PrimeVul + ReposVul + R2Vul, 801 samples across 5 CWE classes

key_numbers.metric: CWE-415 F1 gain (Claude Code, LeanGuard vs Pure LLM)
CWE-416 F1 gain (Codex, LeanGuard vs Pure LLM)
CWE-416 / CWE-415 F1 vs Pure LLM (same DeepSeek-V4-Pro)

structure_gain: LeanGuard (AST-extraction + Lean 4 verification) vs Pure LLM, identical DeepSeek-V4-Pro backend and temperature=0: F1 +0.135 (CWE-416) and +0.191 (CWE-415) (Table IV) -- a clean same-model comparison isolating the neurosymbolic pipeline's contribution.
confound_note: The Pure-LLM-vs-LeanGuard comparison (Table IV) holds the LLM backend fixed, cleanly isolating the pipeline's effect; but the internal 'w/o AST' ablation (RQ2) is confounded because removing AST extraction also changes the LLM's task from filtering candidates to directly identifying guards/dereferences (Section V-D).
stop_detail: The evidence-aware adjudicator (Section IV-G, Table III) grades symbolic (Q_Lean: strong/weak/noisy/none) and neural (Q_LLM: strong/weak/none) verdicts by evidence quality and lets a high-evidence verdict override a low-evidence one (e.g., Lean 'strong' VULNERABLE overrides neural 'none' SAFE) -- this is the paper's core grounding mechanism against premature discharge of safety obligations.
threats_to_datum: Each CWE class requires hand-built extraction rules, property templates, and auto-pairing logic; authors explicitly disclaim generalization to unseen CWE classes; function-level only with no whole-program reasoning; authors describe it as an exploratory prototype, not a deployable tool.
